tests.title: Windows driver / device present
tests.why: Detects missing or unsigned drivers that stop the unit being recognised.
steps: Connect the Twelve MK2 with its USB-C cable directly to the PC (not a hub).
Run the check.
If absent, install the Rane Twelve driver from Rane support and reconnect.

pass.source: Presence is required for operation; see docs/devices/rane-twelve-mk2.md

tests.title: Driver status OK
tests.why: A device with a Code 10/43 error will not enumerate MIDI.
steps: Run the driver check.
Open Device Manager and confirm no warning icon on the Rane Twelve entry.

tests.title: USB enumeration & cable
tests.why: Intermittent disconnects point to cable, port or power faults.
steps: Plug into a rear USB port; try a second port and a different USB-C cable.
Move the platter and tap buttons while watching for disconnect chimes.
Confirm the unit stays in Device Manager / MIDI port list for 2 minutes.

tests.title: Serato DJ Pro detects Twelve MK2
tests.why: Native support requires current Serato DJ Pro.
steps: Install current Serato DJ Pro.
Run the software check; then launch Serato with the Twelve connected.

pass.source: Serato DJ Pro supports the Twelve MK2 natively (Rane product page, unverified wording)

tests.title: DJ software stability
tests.why: Repeated crashes with the controller attached suggest driver or USB problems.
steps: Run the check.

tests.title: MIDI coverage: all controls
tests.why: Finds dead buttons, pads or strip zones and learns unknown messages.
steps: Open the test and touch/press every control once, including shifted functions.
Rotate the platter both ways, touch the strip search end to end, move the pitch fader fully.

tests.title: Unexpected MIDI messages
tests.why: Stray messages while idle indicate noisy sensors.
steps: Hands off the unit for 30 seconds with the platter stopped.

tests.title: Pitch fader sweep & resolution
tests.why: Dirty or worn track causes jumps; resolution determines fine pitch control.
steps: Move the pitch fader slowly end to end and back three times.
Repeat on each pitch range if the range changes the message.

tests.title: Pitch fader resolution (bits)
tests.why: Reports whether 7- or 14-bit; informational as manufacturer value unpublished.
steps: Sweep slowly at the lowest speed you can.

tests.title: Pitch fader jitter at rest
tests.why: Jitter makes tempo wander in software.
steps: Leave the fader at a fixed position for 20 seconds.

tests.title: Platter position resolution (ticks/rev)
tests.why: Low resolution makes scratching feel steppy.
steps: With motor off, turn the platter one slow full revolution clockwise, then one anticlockwise.

tests.title: Platter direction errors
tests.why: Direction flips indicate encoder faults.
steps: Slow revolution each way.

tests.title: Platter touch sensing
tests.why: Needed for scratch mode engage/release.
steps: Touch and release the platter top repeatedly.

tests.title: Buttons: bounce & stuck
tests.why: Chatter causes double triggers.
steps: Press each button 5 times at normal pace.

tests.title: LED feedback
tests.why: Verifies host-to-device MIDI output.
steps: Confirm each lit button/pad changes as the app commands.

tests.title: MIDI timing jitter during platter motion
tests.why: Jitter in platter messages causes uneven scratch feel.
steps: Spin the platter at constant speed (or let the motor run) for 15 seconds.

tests.title: Strip search full length
tests.why: Dead spots on the touch strip prevent track searching.
steps: Slide a finger along the strip end to end slowly, three times.

tests.title: Motor speed 33 1/3 and 45 rpm
tests.why: Speed error causes pitch mismatch vs software deck.
steps: Place a Serato CV02.5 (or 1 kHz-referenced signal source such as a timecode disc under lines) on the platter if a timecode-reading path is available; otherwise use a strobe disc.
Select 33, measure; repeat at 45 with nominalRpm 45.

tests.title: Start-up and brake time
tests.why: Slow start or sticky brake affects mixing and stop effects.
steps: Start and stop the platter with torque on low, then high; repeat 3x.

tests.title: Pitch fader vs actual platter speed
tests.why: Compares ±8/±16/±50 % ranges with measured speed.
steps: Set range ±8 %; move fader to marked positions and measure speed at each.
Repeat in ±16 and ±50 % (scale positions).

tests.title: Warm-up speed drift
tests.why: Drift while motor warms.
steps: Let the platter run 20 minutes.

tests.title: Platter vibration
tests.why: Motor or bearing wear.
steps: Place a phone/probe on the plinth with platter running.

tests.title: Mechanical & visual inspection
tests.why: Platter wobble, loose slipmat, damaged USB port and worn buttons.
steps: Platter sits flat and rotates without rubbing or wobble.
Slipmat/control surface undamaged.
Pitch fader moves smoothly, no crackle.
USB-C port firm in socket.
Rubber feet and housing intact.
No unusual motor noise at either speed.

tests.title: Firmware up to date (Rane/inMusic updater)
tests.why: Outdated firmware can cause missing features with new software.
steps: Open the Rane firmware updater or Serato's device settings.
Note the installed firmware version and whether an update is offered.
Do not unplug during update.

tests.title: Traktor / Virtual DJ MIDI operation
tests.why: Confirms generic MIDI usage works outside Serato.
steps: Open Traktor or VirtualDJ with the device selected.
Confirm platter and pitch move the deck; note mapping source used.
